settings.heading: Stronger than steel, gram for gram
settings.image_alt: Close-up of a bamboo bicycle frame joint showing the natural fibre structure
settings.body: Bamboo's tensile strength reaches around 28,000 PSI — in the same range as mild steel, but at a fraction of the weight. Unlike steel, bamboo is a natural composite: parallel cellulose fibres in a lignin matrix, running the full length of the culm. The same structural principle as carbon fibre, evolved over millions of years. | We tested this with Swansea University. Their three-point flexural bending tests on our actual bamboo tubes confirmed high stiffness and consistent mechanical properties across samples — bamboo behaves like a high-performance engineering material, because it is one.

settings.quote: Woody turned out to be the most reliable bike I've ever owned. I had hardly any mechanical problems on the whole journey and it was a smooth and shock-absorbing ride.
settings.context: 8,288 miles, Colombia to Patagonia, on a BBC-built bamboo frame

settings.heading: A ride you can actually feel
settings.image_alt: Rider on a bamboo bicycle on the open road
settings.body: The fibre structure that makes bamboo strong also makes it comfortable. Those parallel fibres absorb road vibration naturally — something aluminium and steel simply can't match. Less buzz through the handlebars, less fatigue over long distances, a smoother ride on rough roads. | This isn't marketing, it's physics. Bamboo's natural damping has been documented in structural engineering for decades. In a bicycle frame it means you arrive fresher, with less strain on your hands, wrists and back.

settings.quote: Having had it now for about 7 years and ridden it hard — the ride is much smoother than my Cooper. I've ridden over about half of Crete with it.

settings.heading: Why it matters
settings.image_alt: A bamboo frame being built on a jig with simple hand tools
settings.body: To make an aluminium frame you need bauxite mines, smelters running at 1,000°C and factories of CNC machines. Carbon fibre needs petroleum-derived precursors, autoclaves and clean rooms. | To make a bamboo bicycle frame you need bamboo, a jig, hand tools and two days. That's it. | We teach beginners — 95% with zero mechanical experience — to build their own frame in a weekend. Through our Build to Bond programme, frame-building reconnects fathers with their children inside the criminal justice system.

settings.heading: The carbon maths
settings.image_alt: Raw bamboo culms that regrow in 3 to 5 years
settings.body: A peer-reviewed lifecycle analysis by Wageningen University found bamboo bicycle frames have roughly 50% lower environmental impact than aluminium, and about 30% less than steel. | Bamboo reaches structural maturity in 3–5 years; trees take 20–50. It regrows from its root system with no replanting, needs no pesticides or irrigation, and sequesters carbon as it grows. | Most carbon-fibre sports equipment lasts just 3 years and 90% ends up in landfill. A bamboo frame? Still being ridden a decade later.

settings.heading: Ancient material, modern engineering
settings.image_alt: A carbon-and-epoxy lug joint on a bamboo bicycle frame
settings.body: Bamboo has been used structurally for thousands of years — bridges, scaffolding and buildings across Asia, South America and Africa. The first bamboo bicycle was patented in England in 1894 and shown at the London Stanley Cycle Show the same year. | What's changed is the jointing. Carbon-fibre and epoxy connections create joints stronger than the bamboo itself. Combined with precision jigs and heat-treated tubes, the result meets the demands of serious cyclists while staying buildable by complete beginners. | Over 4,000 people in 36+ countries have built with us since 2012 — featured in the Financial Times, BikeRadar and the Design Museum's Cycle Revolution.

settings.quote: I knew nothing about bike maintenance. I thought that if I could be involved in the whole process of putting it together, I'd have a better idea of how to tackle any inevitable breakages. It reminded me how satisfying it is to build something from scratch.
settings.context: 4-day London workshop, road bamboo bike build

settings.question: Does a bamboo bicycle frame crack or split?
settings.answer: Properly treated and sealed bamboo is very stable. Our tubes are heat-treated to remove moisture and sealed with epoxy resin. Store indoors and avoid prolonged exposure to extreme wet conditions.

settings.question: Can I ride a bamboo bike in the rain?
settings.answer: Yes. Finished frames are fully sealed with epoxy resin. Dry your bike after wet rides and store it indoors — the same care you'd give any quality frame.

settings.question: Is bamboo really stronger than steel?
settings.answer: Per unit weight, yes. Bamboo's tensile strength is around 28,000 PSI — in the same range as mild steel — but significantly lighter, giving a superior strength-to-weight ratio. Confirmed by our Swansea University testing.

settings.question: What about the joints?
settings.answer: The joints are the strongest part. Carbon-fibre and epoxy lugs exceed the strength of the bamboo tubes themselves. Our method has been refined over 13 years and 4,000+ builds.

settings.question: How long will a bamboo frame last?
settings.answer: 8–12 years with proper care, with an under-1% failure rate across 4,000+ frames. Many of our 2012 builds are still ridden daily.

settings.question: Do I need experience to build one?
settings.answer: No. 95% of our builders have zero mechanical experience. Workshop frames are completed in 2 days with full expert guidance; home kits include step-by-step instructions and video tutorials.

settings.question: What types of bamboo bicycle can I build?
settings.answer: Any type — road, gravel, mountain, cargo, tandem, balance bike. The geometry is defined by your jig setup, so the design is up to you.

settings.question: Is bamboo a sustainable material for bicycles?
settings.answer: Yes — one of the most sustainable structural materials there is. A peer-reviewed Wageningen University analysis found ~50% lower environmental impact than aluminium. Bamboo matures in 3–5 years, sequesters carbon as it grows, and needs no pesticides or irrigation.
